content:
Measurement in Class 3 brings standard units and conversions for length, weight and capacity — steady-scoring Olympiad content. This guide covers what the Maths Olympiad Class 3 measurement chapter tests, the facts to memorise, and a free 10-question test.

What the Class 3 Maths Olympiad Length, Weight and Capacity chapter tests

  • Length (mm, cm, m, km) and conversions
  • Weight (g, kg)
  • Capacity (mL, L)
  • Adding and subtracting measures with word problems

Key facts your child should know

  • 1 cm = 10 mm; 1 m = 100 cm; 1 km = 1000 m.
  • 1 kg = 1000 g; 1 L = 1000 mL.
  • To convert a bigger unit to a smaller one, multiply; smaller to bigger, divide.
  • Add or subtract the same units, then convert if needed.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Multiplying when you should divide (or vice-versa) in a conversion.
  • Mixing units (adding cm to mm without converting).
  • Forgetting 1 km = 1000 m.

questions.q: Which is lighter: a parcel of 3 kg 75 g or a parcel of 3570 g?
questions.explanation: 3 kg 75 g = 3075 g. Since 3075 g < 3570 g, the 3 kg 75 g parcel is lighter.
Change to cm: 345 cm + 280 cm = 625 cm = 6 m 25 cm.
In metres: 6100 m − 1450 m = 4650 m = 4 km 650 m.

faq.q: How many metres are in a kilometre?
faq.a: One thousand. So 2 km = 2000 m, and 2 km 350 m = 2350 m.
